# Intercomparisons & round robins

The same sample measured in two laboratories rarely gives the same emissivity
at first. The differences come from the method (direct or indirect,
directional or hemispherical), from the heating and temperature measurement,
and from the sample itself, which oxidises while it is being measured.
Intercomparisons turn those differences into shared uncertainty budgets. They
are also the most convincing data an open database like
[EKHI](/data/ekhi.html) can hold: one material, several laboratories, with the
protocol documented.

This page lists the exercises our community runs, from bilateral comparisons
to multi-laboratory round robins. The IR-EMPOWER 2026 round table named them
as one of the community's priorities.

## Current exercises

| Exercise | Participants | Materials | Protocol | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High-temperature emissivity of aeronautical superalloys | [LTeN-CNRS](/network/lten-cnrs.html) · [EHU](/network/thermomat-ehu.html) | Inconel 718 · René 41 · Haynes 25 (discs Ø 20–25 mm, 1–2 mm thick) | Pre-oxidised at 900 °C, then measured in air from 400 to 1000 °C in both laboratories | Samples in preparation |

## Background

The superalloy comparison builds on earlier EHU measurements of the same
alloys, including spectra of samples with a growing oxide film:
[Emissivity measurements on aeronautical alloys](/publications/2010/del-campo/index.html) (2010).
Related work on oxidation and emissivity of these alloy families:

- [Oxidation induced emissivity variations of the Haynes 25 alloy at high temperatures](/publications/2023/balat-pichelin/index.html) (2023)
- [Oxidation in air at 1400 K and optical properties of Inconel 625, FeCrAlloy and Kanthal Super ER](/publications/2020/colas/index.html) (2020)

## Join an exercise

Laboratories that want to take part in an exercise, or propose a new one,
can write through the [contribution form](/contribute/index.html). Results are
published in EKHI with every participant credited.
